meaning: Bits a reader needs per weight of a model trained from scratch, at retained quality (lossy). The rate the thread theorem charges per updated weight when the update is a whole model, as in pretraining.

estimates.context: frontier-scale dense or MoE models, quality within about 1 zero-shot point
estimates.merge: High is the strict within-1%-perplexity standard (4-bit GPTQ/AWQ, SpQR, NVFP4 at 4.03 bits per weight with its 16x16 block scales). Central sits between where zero-shot holds (2 bits, QTIP on Llama 3.1 405B) and where perplexity holds (3 bits); size-optimal fine-tuned rates are 2.0-2.5. Low is QMoE's 0.807 bits/param on an older MoE; a frontier MoE needs about 1.6. Rates that need fine-tuning to decompress are excluded: decompression is itself training.

estimates.context: weights as read by the forward and backward matmuls of a model trained from scratch in low precision; master weights stay FP32/BF16
estimates.merge: Central: NVFP4 weights (16x16 block scales, 4.03 bits) in the largest low-bit runs, Nemotron 3 Ultra (550B total, 55B active, 20T tokens) and Super (120B, 12.7B active, 25T tokens). The loss gap against BF16 is below 0.4% and falls with scale: about 1%, 0.6% and 0.4% at 3B, 8B and 55B active. The final 15% of layers plus attention, latent and embedding projections stay in high precision, which lifts the weight-averaged read to about 5.8. Low: ternary from scratch (BitNet b1.58 2B4T at 4T tokens, Spectra 3.9B, Spectra 1.1 3B at 1.2T), with a fitted loss gap of 5-7% at 15B-330B. 1-bit BitNet reaches 30B but trains on only about 10B tokens. High: FP8 practice (DeepSeek-V3 within 0.25%; FSDP2 float8 weight all-gather). Naive 4-bit weight reads without training-aware quantization cost 5-12%. These are rates of a different training computation, not compressions of a BF16 one: the bound applies to the low-bit run as its own reference circuit, and its master-weight update is extra work the bound does not count.

meaning: Lossless bits per weight of a released checkpoint.

estimates.context: BF16 checkpoints (central, high) and FP8-native ones (low)
estimates.merge: Only the exponent compresses: every BF16 measurement lands at 10.5-10.9 bits (DFloat11 at 70B-405B, ZipNN). FP8-native DeepSeek-R1 gives the low. Lossless coding is an upper bound on b_w, never the attacker's rate.

meaning: Information a trained parameter holds: a ceiling on what a small update can carry per trainable parameter.

estimates.context: memorization and knowledge-capacity experiments, at most about 1.5B parameters
estimates.merge: High: 3.6 bits/param of memorized random data (models of about 100K-20M params). Central: 2 bits/param of extractable knowledge, matching the 2-bit size-optimal quantization rate. Low: the MoE figure.

estimates.context: information a pretrained model's weights carry beyond its registered (seeded) init, per weight
estimates.merge: The registered init saves almost nothing. Restricting pretraining's weights, or their change from init, to rank d/4 costs 7-30% in perplexity at 1B (15.01 with restarts and 18.22 plain, against 13.97 full rank). So the rate relative to init is the model's own information. Central: 2 bits per parameter of extractable knowledge, matching the 2-2.5-bit lossy rates of frontier models. High: the 3.6 bits per parameter memorization ceiling. Low: 0.58 x 2, because a factorized model with 58% of the parameters matches dense loss at equal FLOPs (Spectron, up to 1.5B). Per step, 4-bit weight differences track full-precision training at 6.7B, so per-step novelty is at most 4 bits per parameter, and the cumulative total is capped by capacity rather than by step count.

meaning: Bits per base-model weight of an update relative to committed theta (fine-tuning, RL), at retained quality.

estimates.context: supervised fine-tuning deltas up to 70B
estimates.merge: Values unchanged. Data-free post-hoc codes reach 0.32-0.5 bits per base weight at 7-13B without loss (UltraDelta), between DeltaDQ's data-aware 0.03-0.125 and BitDelta's 1 bit. SFT and distillation deltas lack the rank-1 structure of RL deltas (AlphaRL's controls), so RL rates must not be applied to SFT. High: post-hoc 1-bit codes are near-lossless on chat up to 70B (BitDelta), though they degrade math and code. Central: a random 99% drop at 70B (DARE, about 0.16) and DeltaDQ at 128x (0.125). Low: constrained adapters (VeRA at 13B, 0.003).

estimates.context: RL post-training; the trainer chooses the parametrization
estimates.merge: The central now has two independent supports. Rank-1 LoRA matches full RL on Llama-3.1-8B, and truncating natural RL deltas to rank 1 after training keeps 99.17% of the reasoning gain across 13 models (7B-32B) and 10 algorithms, which is 0.004-0.008 bits per base weight depending on matrix shape. On Qwen3-8B, the best rank-1 LoRA seed matches ranks 16 and 32 but is unreliable across seeds. LoRA RL runs on a 1.04T MoE (Kimi K2) at about 10% of full-RL compute, with no matched full-RL baseline. High: natural RL deltas are dense and full rank, so take the post-hoc 1-bit code. Central: rank-1 LoRA matches full RL on Llama-3.1-8B (3M params, as a rate per base weight). Low: TinyLoRA's 10k parameters on Qwen-7B (13 parameters is the extreme, Qwen-specific). RL sparsity (68-96% unchanged) is treated as a precision artifact that does not lower b_w.

meaning: Description length of a whole update. The policy charges a block for the part of it the block must read; an update under K/2 that a block can also decode fits in one block.

estimates.context: RL post-training of a frontier model, smallest parametrization that works
estimates.merge: Low: TinyLoRA-scale adapters (0.01 MB). Central: 1-10 MB, the size of K; R1-Zero's 5.3M episodes bound its reward information at about 0.66 MB. High: rank-1 LoRA on every expert of a 1T MoE, 1.27 GB in bf16 (derived from the Kimi K2 config).

estimates.context: a whole zeroth-order or evolution-strategies run, as seeds and scalars
estimates.merge: Central: MeZO stores a 20k-step fine-tune of a 66B model in under 0.1 MB. Low: an intrinsic-dimension subspace. High: NOLA at 70B.

estimates.context: agentic coding RL on a frontier-size model, smallest parametrization demonstrated to work
estimates.merge: Low: Mehta's rank-32 LoRA if only attention and shared experts carry adapters. Central: TRACE's 1.6B-parameter adapter in bf16, and Mehta's mid reading. High: full-parameter RL on a 1T model in bf16, which Kimi K2 does.

meaning: Work to regenerate one seed-step's perturbation and add it, per parameter.

estimates.context: Gaussian or Rademacher noise from a counter-based PRNG, plus an add
estimates.merge: Derived: rebuilding MeZO's weights needs no forward pass or data, only one noise draw and one multiply-add per parameter per step. In Boolean gates it is about 1e2-1e5 per parameter, which would make decoding the binding cost.

meaning: Fraction of parameters an update changes materially.

estimates.context: fine-tuning and RL deltas
estimates.merge: Low: trained-in sparsity (diff pruning). Central: the top 20% of a delta suffices (TIES); MoE fine-tuning touches 5-15% of experts. High: SFT changes 81-99% of weights. An arbitrary mask costs H(phi) bits per weight, so sparsity lowers b_w only when positions are free (seeded, or whole experts).

meaning: Aggregate update every replica applies per step in working low-communication pretraining: an achieved rate, so an upper bound on a frontier update's per-step information.

estimates.context: DiLoCo-family runs at 0.5B-72B
estimates.merge: Low: Streaming DiLoCo. Central: INTELLECT-1, MuLoCo and SparseLoCo-family runs. High: DisTrO without re-quantized all-reduce. At N = 1e12 even the low is 4e10 bits per step, thousands of times K.

meaning: Per-worker, per-step communication reduction against a dense bf16 all-reduce. These methods shrink traffic between workers that each hold a full model, so they do not by themselves evade a per-block cap.

estimates.context: matched-loss results at 1B-72B
estimates.merge: Low: DiLoCo at 10B (over 100x), MuLoCo, INTELLECT-1. Central: SparseLoCo at matched loss (889x), DisTrO. High: SparseLoCo with a loss penalty. Error feedback keeps the discarded part in dense worker-local state, so the information moves rather than disappears.

meaning: Bits per activation entry crossing a block boundary in training, at retained quality. Every bound and the sharding floor scale with it.

estimates.context: residual-stream activations sent between pipeline stages in training; bits per original d_model entry (activation.boundary_bits / d_model), a learned bottleneck folded in
estimates.merge: High: production systems send 8-bit activations across parallel links (DeepSeek-V3 FP8 dispatch at d = 7168, SWARM, Petals); Megatron pipelines send BF16. Central: TAH-Quant, stable from about 4.4 bits at 3B or less, the largest matched-loss boundary test. Learned per-stage Stiefel projections reach 8x (2 bits per original entry) at 1B on 20 tokens per parameter for +1.4-2.0% loss, but a fixed random subspace at 8x costs 5.9% and the Subspace Networks recipe 14-26%, so 2 bits is method-specific and lossy. Low: MAPL with residual VQ at 16x, about 1 bit per original entry, +2.3-3.0% at 1B, with projectors and codebooks held by both stages; Subspace Networks' 100x (0.16 bits) at 8B is set aside because a matched-token replication of its method loses 14-26% at only 8x. Negative: Optimus-CC's forward inter-stage compression diverged even at low rates; no sub-8-bit forward boundary result exists above 3B, so at scale 8 bits is what is defensible and 4 is a small-model figure. Backward traffic needs about 1.5-2x the forward bits under quantization (AQ-SGD, TAH-Quant, Rudakov); early-layer boundaries need more than late ones (Bian).

estimates.context: forward activations at linear-layer GEMM inputs in pretraining, scales included (not the tensors sent between blocks)
estimates.merge: Central: NVFP4 (E2M1 plus an E4M3 scale per 16) on Fprop inputs ends 1.5% above FP8 at 12B on 10T tokens and within 0.4% of BF16 branches at 550B total / 55B active on 20T, with 15-16% of layers kept in BF16 in both (derived average about 6.2 bits including them). Low: FP4 with one scale per token costs 4.8% at 7-13B on 100B tokens and needs a 0.2-6% high-precision outlier side channel; MXFP4 (4.25) is 2.5% worse than FP8 at 12B. High: FP8 practice, 8 bits per-tensor (Nemotron-H 56B / 20T, under 0.1%) to 8.25 with 1x128 scales (DeepSeek-V3 671B / 14.8T and Ling-1T / 900B, under 0.25%). Conflict: NVIDIA's 4-bit gap shrinks with scale (1% at 3B active, 0.6% at 8B, 0.4% at 55B) while QAT laws and Wang's 1.3B-13B runs find it grows with tokens per parameter; we take the at-scale runs.

estimates.context: activation-gradients at backward GEMM inputs (Dgrad and Wgrad) in pretraining, scales included
estimates.merge: Central: NVFP4 activation-gradients with stochastic rounding (and 16x16 Hadamard transforms on Wgrad inputs) at 12B / 10T, and NVFP4 Dgrad and Wgrad in Nemotron 3 Ultra at 550B / 20T. Low: MXFP4 with a random Hadamard transform and stochastic rounding matches BF16 at 1.3B / 210B tokens, with a BF16 forward. High: E5M2 per-tensor at 56B / 20T (Nemotron-H); E4M3 with 1x128 scales is 8.25 (DeepSeek-V3, Ling-1T). The bits equal the forward pass's only with unbiased rounding: round-to-nearest MXFP4 backward costs 3.4% at 1.3B. Conflict: on links between blocks, where nothing is rounded stochastically, gradients need about 1.5-2x the forward bits (Rudakov 6 vs 2-4, TAH-Quant 6-8 vs 4.4), while Optimus-CC's low-rank code finds the reverse (forward diverged; backward 10x lossless on epilogue micro-batches at 8.3B). This estimate takes the GEMM-input runs.

estimates.context: tensor-parallel partial sums in reduce-scatter or all-reduce, forward and backward, in pretraining; bits per entry at full shard width, scales included, a learned bottleneck folded in
estimates.merge: Central: FP8 with two scales per 256-entry block after an RMS rescale and Hadamard rotation costs +0.70% at GPT-6.7B and +0.03% at Qwen2.5-7B in 10,000-iteration runs (TACO); MegaScale-MoE sends forward partial sums as per-token FP8 and sums them in FP32 at 35B-176B MoE, gap unquantified. High: practice keeps forward partial sums in BF16 (FP8-LM's forward reduce-scatter, DeepSeek-V3's combine, NVFP4's communication). Low: a learned linear encoder before the all-reduce sums partial sums at 100 of 1024 dims (derived 1.6 bits per original entry) in BERT-Large 345M, last layers only, within about 3% on most tasks; the lowest quantizer is Echo's 4.25 bits with error feedback, high-precision summation and a raised LR, +0.9% at 0.6B / 10B tokens. Negative: per-tensor FP8 and INT8 diverge on TP tensors and E5M2 costs 24% (TACO); every working scheme dequantizes before summing (MegaScale-MoE, ZeRO++). Inference partial sums take 5.2 bits at 70-123B for +0.5-1.7% and INT4 in the reduce step (FlashComm).

meaning: Bits per KV-cache entry at retained quality (inference).

estimates.context: KV-cache quantization
estimates.merge: Central: KIVI's 2 bits. Low: coupled and low-rank KV methods. High: production 4-bit KV.

meaning: Bits per token crossing a shard boundary at d_model = 7168: effective width times b_a. Sets the sharding floor w_cut / b_tok.

estimates.context: attacker's choice of architecture and codec at d_model = 7168
estimates.merge: High: production practice, d at 8 bits. Central: a bottleneck retrained to 0.5 d at 4 bits (a linear d/2 bottleneck costs SWARM 26-28% more steps; ESPACE projects to 0.25 d at +0.18 perplexity). Low: Subspace Networks' claimed 100x (0.01 d at 16 bits), one preprint whose matched-token replication loses 14-26% in loss at only 8x. A standard architecture at FP4 is 28672. An unmodified model's boundary activations are not low-rank.

meaning: Bits per prompt token the policy allows for.

estimates.context: raw token ids of frontier tokenizers (128k-200k vocabularies)
estimates.merge: log2 of the vocabulary: Llama 3 (128,256) to o200k (about 200,019). None reaches 20 bits.

estimates.context: arithmetic-coded against a strong committed base model
estimates.merge: Central: Llama-3.1-405B and DeepSeek-V3 at about 0.54 bits/byte on Pile-test, times 3.94 characters per token. Low: Python code. High: 7-8B models (LLMZip). Requires bit-exact probabilities, which exact circuits give.

meaning: Prompt compression at retained task quality. Soft-prompt 'compression' cuts positions, not bits: each vector input must be charged as an activation.

estimates.context: token-dropping and learned compressors
estimates.merge: LLMLingua-2 2-5x and ICAE 4x (central), LLMLingua 20x and gist tokens 26x (high, narrower tasks). 480-1568x soft compression keeps only 62-73% of capability and is not a bit ratio.

meaning: Size of the new information behind a measured capability gain: the shared headroom one block keeps.

estimates.context: RL with tiny adapters, measured gains on math at 7-8B
estimates.merge: Low: 26 bytes of TinyLoRA add 15 points. Central: 20 KB. High: rank-1 LoRA on an 8B model (6 MB) matches full RL. Mostly Qwen math models, which run high; all elicitation of existing skill.

estimates.context: small curated SFT sets
estimates.merge: LIMA's 1,000 examples (94 KB), about 1 MB for ReFT-scale sets, s1's 1k traces (7.7 MB).

estimates.context: prompts and context playbooks
estimates.merge: OPRO's three words (GSM8K 34% to 80%), URIAL's 2 KB, ACE playbooks and many-shot ICL at 0.2-1 MB.

meaning: Compute a BF16 run needs to reach the loss of a pretraining run at rates (b_w, b_a), divided by that run's compute (FLOPs = 6ND, MACs counted once whatever their precision). 1 for BF16; below 1 when compressed training needs more compute. Pretraining efficiency under the policy is max m / rho.

estimates.context: FP8 weights and activations in every block GEMM, forward and backward; master weights FP16/FP32
estimates.merge: Equal loss at equal tokens at 7B-175B (FP8-LM) and 8B (all GEMMs incl. attention, FOG); 56B on 20T tokens in FP8 (Nemotron-H). Low allows for the architecture changes FP8 attention needs.

estimates.context: 4-bit weights and activations in the linear-layer GEMMs (forward; NVFP4 and Quartet also the backward GEMMs), at a Chinchilla-optimal 1e25 FLOP
estimates.merge: Central: the unified-law capacity 0.85 (forward-only QAT, 200M, m = rho under its effective-parameter form) and the at-scale NVFP4 anchors, 0.72-0.79 derived from <0.4% and <0.6% loss gaps at 55B and 8B active (Hoffmann law, tokens-equivalent at fixed N; these are lower bounds). Low: Quartet's fwd+bwd FP4 0.62 and Chen's additive law extrapolated to 1e25 (0.56). The 12B NVFP4 run at 830 tokens/parameter (1.5% gap, m ~ 0.38) and Kumar's naive integer quantizer (0.23) are excluded as over-trained and superseded. High: the unified-law single-tensor 4-bit values (0.90, 0.91).

estimates.context: 4-bit forward weights, 16-bit activations, 1e25 FLOP
estimates.merge: Central: unified-law W4A16 0.90 and Chen W4A16 0.86 at 1e25 (extrapolated). Low: Sun's FP4 E2M1 weight law extrapolated to 1e25 (0.48; 0.81 at 1e21), whose penalty grows as D^0.52/N^0.24. High: a full-precision phase then weight QAT is near-lossless at 4 bits (Dremov).

estimates.context: ternary (1.58-bit) forward weights, 8-16-bit activations, latent weights high precision
estimates.merge: Central: unified-law capacity interpolated at 0.58 of the way from 1 to 2 bits (Gaussian MSE), 0.35; Spectra's fixed-300B-token laws give 0.32 at 3.9B; Spectra 1.1's two laws give 0.23 at 1e21 FLOP. Low: Spectra 1.1 extrapolated past 1e22 collapses (0.02 at 1e25) on a 0.02 floor gap, discounted. High: BitNet's gap narrows with N.

estimates.context: full-rank weights trained through low-rank optimizer updates or merged low-rank adapters (GaLore, Fira, LTE), from scratch
estimates.merge: Low: GaLore at 1B vs tuned full-rank, 0.40 derived from perplexity-vs-FLOPs (Glentis Table 3). Central: LTE needs 40% more samples (0.71, ViT-S) and Fira 0.52 at 1B. High: GaLore 2 matches full-rank at 7B on 500B tokens.

estimates.context: 2-bit weights and activations in the forward GEMMs, extrapolated to a Chinchilla-optimal 1e25 FLOP
estimates.merge: Central and high: the unified-law capacity at W2A2, 0.30 (forward-only QAT at 30M-200M, m = rho under its effective-parameter form). Low: QuEST's eff(2) = 0.16 with weights and activations tied. Kumar's law predicts divergence at 2-bit activations. No run near this cell exists above 1.6B, so it is an extrapolation in scale and in method.

estimates.context: 1-bit weights and activations in the forward GEMMs, extrapolated to a Chinchilla-optimal 1e25 FLOP
estimates.merge: Central and high: the unified-law capacity at W1A1, 0.09. Low: QuEST's eff(1) = 0.02. Kumar's law predicts divergence. An extrapolation in scale and method, kept to show where the attacker's gain stops.

meaning: Compute spent on RL post-training divided by the base model's pretraining compute.

estimates.context: reasoning and agentic RL on frontier and near-frontier models, 2025
estimates.merge: Low: smallest disclosed share for a competitive reasoning model (Llama-Nemotron Ultra <1%; DeepSeek-R1-Zero 3.8%). Central: the largest first-party measurement, DeepSeek-V3.2 'already exceeds 10%'. High: stated frontier practice without numbers, Grok 4 RL 'at pretraining scale', o3 at 10x o1. Epoch's 20% for R1 is set aside: it implies about 5x the GPU-hours DeepSeek reported.

meaning: Fraction of a model's measured gain over its pretrained base that RL training accounts for.

estimates.context: share of DeepSeek-R1's gain over DeepSeek-V3 reproduced by pure RL (R1-Zero) on the same 671B base, per benchmark
RL's own boost at matched output tokens as a share of a reasoning model's total gain over its base (Claude 3.7 vs 3.5 Sonnet)
estimates.merge: Ord: OTIS Mock AIME 4/49, MATH level 5 6/34, GPQA Diamond 9/24; the remainder is inference scaling that RL unlocks. Consistent with Epoch's even log split of a ~10x CEG.

meaning: Fraction of full-weight RL's measured gain kept when RL's trainable state is at most about 2e7 bits.

estimates.context: RLVR on math, 1.5B-32B bases
estimates.merge: Retention favours the attacker, so high is the attacker's best. Low: rank-1 LoRA (about 1.8e7 bits) on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B keeps 0%. Central: TinyLoRA keeps about 90% with 1000x fewer parameters at 7-8B; rank-1 LoRA (about 4e7 bits at 8B) matches full RL. High: AlphaRL's post-hoc rank-1 truncation keeps 99% at 7-32B (about 1e8 bits at 32B).

estimates.context: agentic coding and SWE RL on a 100B-1T model
estimates.merge: No measurement at about 2e7 bits exists above 32B or for agentic RL. The smallest state shown to work at 1T is a rank-32 LoRA of at least 2.7e9 bits, with no full-weight baseline; TRACE uses 2.6e10 bits per adapter at 30B; Yin's retention rises with rank (0 at rank 1, 0.77 at rank 16); Kimi K2 itself uses full-parameter RL. Central splits the elicitation reading from the rank-floor reading.

meaning: RL compute at 90% of the fitted asymptotic gain divided by the compute at half the gain, for a fixed base and task set.

estimates.context: ScaleRL sigmoid fits, 8B dense and 17Bx16 MoE, math RLVR
estimates.merge: 9^(1/B) with fitted B = 1.92 (8B, 14k), 1.89 (8B, 32k), 1.65 (Scout). Not a cap on total frontier RL: adding environments raises the asymptote.
